 Loans The best online personal loans of 2026
 Online lenders can provide convenience and more flexible eligibility criteria than traditional banks.
 Published Thu, Nov 5 2026 Dan Avery Updates editor, CNBC Select Jasmin Suknanan Lead Reporter, CNBC Select Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Online banks and fintech lenders now originate roughly 45% of unsecured personal loans in the U.S., according to data from credit reporting bureau TransUnion . 
 Digital platforms can offer borrowers more convenience and faster funding times than brick-and-mortar institutions, and also frequently have more flexible eligibility criteria.
 CNBC Select has chosen the best online personal loan lenders, looking at affordability, fees, repayment terms, funding times, eligibility requirements and other criteria. For more on how we made our selections, read our methodology .
 Best online personal loans 
 Best for bad (or no) credit:   Upstart 
 Best for larger loans:   SoFi 
 Best for fast funding : OneMain Financial 
 Best for no fees : Discover Loans 
 Best for low rates: Rocket Loans 
 Best for debt consolidation: Happy Money 
 Best for secured loans : Best Egg 
 Best for fair credit: Prosper 
 Best for bad (or no) credit: Upstart
 Who's this for? Upstart considers applicants with a 300 FICO Score, the lowest possible, as well as borrowers with limited or no credit history . Instead of only relying on traditional credit scores, its AI-powered underwriting platform examines thousands of variables, including job history, earning potential, highest level of education and debt-to-income ratio . 
 Standout benefits: You can be approved for as little as $1,000 and most loans are funded by the next business day.
 Upstart Personal Loans
 Learn More Learn More Spotlight
 Designed for applicants with low or no credit score. 
 Upstart considers applicants with FICO Scores of 300 (the lowest possible) and those with insufficient credit history.
 See if you're pre-approved for a personal loan offer. 
 Credit score Bad 300–580 
 Terms 36 and 60 months
 Loan amounts $1,000 to $75,000
 Annual Percentage Rate (APR) 6.30% - 35.99%
 Our expert take
 We like that Upstart considers factors besides credit score, including education, income and employment history. However, co-signers aren't accepted.
 Pros & cons
 Accept applicants with bad or no credit 
 Minimum APR is lower than many competitors'
 Approves personal loans up to $75,000
 Most loans are funded the next business day
 Origination fee of 0% to 10% 
 Doesn't allow co-signers or co-borrowers
 Best for larger loans: SoFi
 Who's this for?   SoFi  approves loans of up to $100,000, more than most lenders. You can lower your APR by setting up automatic payment or by choosing direct pay for debt consolidation loans .
 Standout benefits: Origination fees are optional and may result in a lower rate. Same-day funding is often available if you sign your loan agreement by 5:30 p.m. ET on a business day. 
 SoFi Personal Loans
 Learn More Learn More Spotlight
 Best if you need a larger loan. 
 SoFi approves loans for as much as $100,000, with no origination or application fee.
 See if you're pre-approved for a personal loan offer. 
 Credit score Good to Excellent 670–850 
 Terms 24 to 84 months
 Loan amounts $5,000 to $100,000
 Annual Percentage Rate (APR) 6.49% to 35.49% when you sign up for autopay
 Our expert take
 We like that SoFi has high loan caps and doesn't charge any origination fee, so borrowers get the full amount funded. The credit requirements can be stringent, however, and interest rates for weaker applicants are on the higher side. 
 Pros & cons
 Loans approved for up to $100,000
 No origination fee or late fee
 Next-day funding available
 Accepts co-borrowers
 Minimum loan amount is $5,000
 High APR for fair/low credit
 More details
 Fixed rates from 6.99% APR to 35.49% APR reflect the 0.25% autopay interest rate discount and a 0.25% member rate discount. SoFi rate ranges are current as of 11/4/26 and are subject to change without notice. The average of SoFi Personal Loans funded in 2024 was around $33K. Not all applicants qualify for the lowest rate. Lowest rates reserved for the most creditworthy borrowers. Your actual rate will be within the range of rates listed and will depend on the term you select, evaluation of your creditworthiness, income, and a variety of other factors. 
 Best for fast funding: OneMain Financial
 Who's this for? OneMain Financial approves personal loans for up to $35,000 with funding available as fast as one hour after closing, if disbursed via debit card. 
 Standout benefits: OneMain Financial does not have a specific minimum FICO score and often considers applicants with scores at or below 580. It also allows borrowers to apply with a co-borrower or use their vehicle as collateral. 
 OneMain Financial Personal Loans
 Learn More Learn More Spotlight
 Good for secured personal loans. 
 OneMain Financial allows borrowers to use their vehicle as collateral to improve approval odds and unlock better rates and larger loan amounts.
 See if you're pre-approved for a personal loan offer. 
 Credit score Limited to Fair None–670 
 Terms 24 to 60 months
 Loan amounts $1,500 to $30,000
 Annual Percentage Rate (APR) 11.99% to 35.99%
 Our expert take
 We like that OneMain accepts borrowers with bad credit and offers secured loans and fast funding. However, its minimum APR is on the high side and the $30,000 financing maximum may be too low if you need a larger loan.
 Pros & cons
 Approves applicants with bad/fair credit
 Same-day funding available 
 Can apply with collateral
 Co-applicants allowed
 High origination fee
 High minimum interest rate
 No autopay discount
 More details
 *You must complete a loan application and continue to meet any criteria used to select you for a loan offer. Not all applicants are approved.  Loan approval and actual loan terms depend on applicant's state of residence and ability to meet OneMain Financial credit standards such as a responsible credit history, sufficient income after monthly expenses, and if applicable, availability of eligible collateral. 
 Not all approved applicants qualify for larger loan amounts, lower APRs, or the most favorable loan terms.  For example, larger loan amounts typically require a first lien on a motor vehicle that is no more than ten years old, meets our value requirements, and is titled in applicant's name with valid insurance. APRs are generally higher on loans not secured by a vehicle.  
 Example Loan:  A $6,000 loan with a 24.99% APR that is repayable in 60 monthly installments would have monthly payments of $176.07. 
 OneMain charges origination fees allowed by law.  Depending on the state where the loan is opened, the origination fee may be either a flat amount or a percentage of the loan amount. Flat fees vary by state, ranging from $25 to $500. Percentage-based fees vary by state, ranging from 1% to 10% of the loan amount subject to certain state limits on the fee amount.  
 For information about these fees and minimum and maximum loan sizes available in certain states, visit  omf.com/loanfees . 
 Current OneMain Customers:  Loan offers presented to a consumer assume the individual has no active loan with OneMain or one of its affiliates. If a customer applies for a new loan offer, a OneMain representative will discuss available options. 
 Active-duty military, their spouse or dependents covered by the Military Lending Act (MLA) may not pledge any vehicle as collateral.  If you are covered by the MLA, you are not eligible for secured loans.Loan proceeds cannot be used for postsecondary educational expenses as defined by the CFPB's Regulation Z such as college, university or vocational expense; for any business or commercial purpose; to purchase cryptocurrency assets, securities, derivatives or other speculative investments; or for gambling or illegal purposes.
 Time to Fund Loans:  Funding within one hour after loan closing through SpeedFunds® must be disbursed to a bank-issued debit card. Disbursement by check or ACH may take up to 1-2 business days after closing. 
 Best for no fees: Discover Loans
 Who's this for?  Online lenders are more likely to attach upfront fees than traditional brick-and-mortar banks, but Discover doesn't charge an origination fee. There's also no late fee if your payment isn't on time. 
 Standout benefits: If you use the funds for debt consolidation, Discover will send payments directly to your creditors.
 Discover Personal Loans

 Designed to get you funded fast. 
 Discover offers same-day decisions in most instances and can get you funded as soon as the next business day.

 Terms 36, 48, 60, 72 and 84 months
 Loan amounts $2,500 to $40,000
 Annual Percentage Rate (APR) 6.99% - 24.99%
 Our expert take
 Discover personal loans come with fairly high credit score requirements, but have no origination or late fees and funding is available in as little as one business day. That makes them a great option iff you have good credit.

 Discover will pay creditors directly if you have a debt consolidation loan
 Funds may be available as soon as the next business day.
 No autopay discount.
 No joint applications.

 Standout benefits: Same-day funding is often available if you sign your loan agreement by 4 p.m. ET.

 Best for debt consolidation: Happy Money
 Who's this for?  Happy Money 's Payoff Loan™ is a debt consolidation loan aimed at swapping high-interest credit card bills with a single monthly payment with a lower fixed APR. According to Happy Money, borrowers who pay off at least $5,000 in credit card bills with a Payoff Loan see an average increase of 40 points on their FICO Score.
 Standout benefits: Happy Money approves borrowers with a FICO Score of 620, making it a good option if you have fair credit. Borrowers can repay their loan in terms ranging from 24 to 84 months.
 Happy Money

 Happy Money's Payoff Loan is a solid option for consolidating credit card bills. It offers borrowers with fair credit flexible repayment terms and the option to have Happy Money pay your creditors directly. The $5,000 minimum may be high for your needs, though, and the origination fee can run from 2% to 12%, which is deducted from your loan proceeds.

 Best for secured loans: Best Egg
 Who's this for? Best Egg allows secured loans using the fixtures in your home as collateral, including cabinetry, light fixtures and HVAC systems. You can also use the value of your car, RV or other vehicle as to secure a vehicle equity loan. According to Best Egg, securing your loan can lower your APR by 20% compared to one of its unsecured loans.
 Standout benefits: Best Egg considers applicants with a FICO Score of 600, making it good for borrowers with fair credit. For debt consolidation loans , it will send payments directly to up to 10 different creditors.

 Standout benefits : Prosper accepts co-borrowers. Once your loan is funded through the marketplace, you may be able to get your money as soon as the next business day.

 How to compare online loans
 One of the perks of an online loan is being able to prequalify and see estimated rates, terms and loan amounts without hurting your credit. 
 Use that opportunity to shop around to find the best offer by looking at:
 APR: The annual percentage rate (APR) includes the interest rate and certain upfront fees, giving you a clearer sense of the overall cost of borrowing.  
 Available loan amounts: Lenders have minimum and maximum limits on personal loans, so make sure you can get the amount you need. Many lenders cap loans at $50,000 but some may go up to  $100,000 or higher,  Minimums can be anywhere from a few hundred to $5,000. Going with a lender with a higher minimum could mean borrowing more than you need.
 Repayment terms: Loan terms typically range from 24 to 60 months, or 2 to 5 years. If you need more flexibility, look for a provider with a longer timeline.  
 Fees: Online lenders are more likely to charge an origination fee, but you can find providers that don't. Look at other charges, as well, like late fees and prepayment penalties. 
 Eligibility requirements: Review minimum credit score, income and debt-to-income requirements before submitting an application. Make sure the lender operates in your state and check if there are restrictions on what the loan can be used for . 
 Funding speed: If you need money quickly, compare lenders' estimated approval and funding timelines. Keep in mind, your approval and funding speed may vary if you need to provide additional documentation.   
 Customer support: An online lender may have a better mobile or web interface but lack robust personal service. If that's important to you, look for providers with phone, chat and email options.   
 Reputation: Research a lender's reputation by checking online reviews, the Better Business Bureau and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
 How to apply for a personal loan online
 Applying for a personal loan online can be convenient, but you'll need to have some information and documents ready.
 1. Check your credit score. Review your credit report and score before applying. Your credit history can influence your eligibility, interest rate and loan terms.
 2. Gather the necessary documentation. Depending on the lender, you may need to submit a government-issued ID, proof of income and bank account details. 
 3. Prequalify for loan offers. If you can, prequalify with a lender to get an estimate of the rates and terms you'll be offered, without a hard credit inquiry.
 4. Complete the online application. Once you have chosen your lender, you should be able to upload your personal and financial information and select your desired loan amount. The lenders on this list are often able to approve applicants within minutes, although an incomplete application may slow down the process.
 5. Review and accept the loan offer. Before signing the loan agreement, make sure you're comfortable with the APR, total repayment amount, monthly payment and repayment schedule.
 6. Receive your funds and begin repayment. After you accept, the lender should deposit the money directly into your bank account. If you sign early enough on a business day, most lenders on this list are able to provide funding the same or next day. With a debt consolidation loan, they may be able to pay your creditors directly.
 Pros and cons of online loans
 Pros Can easily get prequalified and compare rates.
 Approval and funding can happen within a single business day. 
 Often have more flexible credit and income requirements.
 Cons No physical branches for in-person service.
 More likely to charge an origination fee.
 Maximum APRs can reach 36% or more for riskier borrowers.
 Fewer financial products available.
 Are online loans safe?
 An online loan can be as safe as one from a traditional bank, but it's important to thoroughly vet the lender before sharing personal information or signing any loan agreement.
 Some digital-only institutions, like SoFi and Happen Bank, are nationally chartered banks. They're required to follow the same federal and state laws that apply to traditional brick-and-mortar institutions and deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. 
 Others are nonbank lenders that operate as financial platforms, partnering with chartered banks that originate their loans.
 An online lender should be transparent about interest rates, fees, repayment terms, monthly payments and other loan information. Watch out for predatory practices, like APRs above 36%, and be wary of lenders that guarantee approval or demand an upfront payment in exchange for a loan. 
 Legitimate lenders may charge application or origination fees, but they don't guarantee approval. 
 You can look lenders up on registries like the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System or FDIC BankFind , read independent reviews and ratings, and check complaints with the Better Business Bureau and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
 FAQs
 What do you need to apply for a personal loan online?
 In most cases, applicants must have a valid U.S. Social Security number, address and government-sponsored ID, and provide proof of steady income. You'll also need to provide bank account and routing numbers, so the funds can be deposited if you're approved.
 Can I get an online loan with bad credit?
 Yes, there are a number of online lenders that specialize in borrowers with bad credit, including OneMain Financial and Avant . 
 You can also improve your chances of approval by securing your loan with collateral or applying with a co-borrower.
 Does prequalifying for an online loan hurt my credit score?
 No, prequalification involves a soft credit inquiry , which allows you to get estimated rates, terms and loan amounts without lowering your credit score. If you formally accept a loan offer, the lender will typically require a hard credit inquiry, which can lower your score by a few points temporarily.

 Our methodology
 To determine which online personal loans were the best, CNBC Select reviewed more than two dozen online banks, credit unions, and lending platforms.
 To narrow down our list, we focused on the following features:
 APR: We considered each lender's interest rates and the overall cost of borrowing.
 Fees: We considered whether a lender charged origination fees, late fees or returned-payment fees. None of the lenders on this list assess a prepayment penalty.
 Loan terms: We gave more weight to lenders offering a broader range of repayment terms.
 Loan amounts: We considered the minimum and maximum loan amounts available from each lender.
 Eligibility requirements: When possible, we considered the credit score and debt-to-income ratio needed for loan approval. We also considered whether lenders allowed co-signers or secured loans.
 Funding speed: We prioritized lenders that made funds available the same or next business day. For debt consolidation loans, we also considered whether lenders paid creditors directly.
 Discounts: We considered whether lenders offered rate reductions for autopay, existing customers, or direct payment to creditors for debt consolidation loans.
 Transparency: We considered whether lenders clearly disclosed rates, fees, eligibility requirements, and loan terms on their websites.
 Customer experience: We gave more weight to lenders with evening and weekend customer service hours, easy-to-navigate websites and mobile interfaces, and online chat.
 Lender reputation: We reviewed Better Business Bureau ratings and third-party reviews from sites like Trustpilot. We also considered whether lenders had faced legal or regulatory action.
 Availability: We gave more weight to lenders that operate in all or most U.S. states.
 We also considered CNBC Select audience data when available, such as general demographics and engagement with our content and tools.
